title: Displacement response is shifting from short-term relief toward work, enterprise, social protection, and national-system inclusion
source_unit: ILO PROSPECTS: Results at a glance, September 2026, published 24 September 2026
geography: PROSPECTS partnership work with forcibly displaced persons and host communities across participating country programmes

observations.period: 2018–2027; PROSPECTS partnership phase and institutional coalition

denominator.unit: core international partners named in the PROSPECTS partnership

partners.value: Government of the Netherlands, IFC, ILO, UNHCR, UNICEF, and World Bank are named as the partnership actors

programme_horizon.value: the partnership was launched in 2018 and is in its second phase through 2027

response_shift.value: PROSPECTS supports a shift from short-term humanitarian assistance toward longer-term development-centred solutions

observations.method: ILO summarizes a multi-agency partnership and its contribution to longer-term solutions for displaced people and host communities.
observations.uncertainty: The partnership description does not provide a complete country-by-country reach, counterfactual, or causal estimate of durable inclusion.
observations.subgroup: Forcibly displaced persons, refugees, host communities, national institutions, employers, workers' organizations, and local economic actors.
observations.counterinterpretation: A longer programme horizon can support systems change, but humanitarian needs may remain acute and long-term development approaches may not reach people excluded from formal systems.

decent_work.value: ILO works with governments, employers, and workers' organizations to advance decent work and include forcibly displaced persons and host communities in national labour markets

skills.value: skills development is a named inclusion mechanism

employment.value: employment access is a named inclusion mechanism

standards.value: the approach is grounded in international labour standards

observations.method: The brief describes institutional and labour-market pathways for inclusion rather than only humanitarian delivery.
observations.uncertainty: Named pathways do not establish employment rates, job quality, legal work access, earnings, or parity between displaced and host populations.
observations.subgroup: Displaced workers, host-community workers, employers, trade unions, labour ministries, training providers, and informal workers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Labour-market inclusion can improve autonomy and social connection, but weak demand, documentation barriers, informality, discrimination, and local job scarcity can limit gains.

national_systems.value: strengthening national systems and institutions is central to addressing shared and evolving needs

social_protection.value: social protection is a named mechanism for inclusion

local_economy.value: local economic development and access to enterprise opportunities are named mechanisms

observations.method: ILO frames inclusion through public systems, social protection, local economic development, and enterprise opportunities for displaced and host populations.
observations.uncertainty: The framework does not provide a national-system capacity score, benefit-coverage estimate, or evidence that all participating systems are durable or inclusive.
observations.subgroup: Displaced households, host communities, public agencies, small enterprises, entrepreneurs, social-protection administrators, and local economic institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: System integration can reduce parallelism, but national systems may themselves be underfunded, exclusionary, or unable to absorb additional demand.

denominator.unit: PROSPECTS shared-needs and host-community outcome frame

shared_needs.value: the partnership addresses shared and evolving needs of refugees and host communities

inclusive_society.value: the partnership contributes to more inclusive societies

coordination.value: governments, employers' and workers' organizations, and international partners are connected in implementation

observations.method: The brief links displaced-person inclusion to host-community conditions and multi-actor institutional cooperation.
observations.uncertainty: An inclusive-society contribution is a programme objective and framing, not a measured change in belonging, social cohesion, or host-community attitudes.
observations.subgroup: Refugees, internally displaced and other forcibly displaced people where covered by programmes, host residents, employers, workers' organizations, and public institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: Shared programming may support cohesion, but competition over jobs, services, housing, or political attention can still produce local tension.

related_sources.claim: Complementary ILO global labour-market and decent-work context.
Complementary UNICEF framework on children affected by migration and displacement.

boundary: This record adds an implementation and labour-market route linking forced displacement, host communities, decent work, skills, employment, enterprise, social protection, national systems, and inclusive-society goals. It uses a public programme results brief, not respondent-level employment histories, a complete beneficiary census, job-quality or earnings estimates, causal programme evaluation, representative host-community attitudes, or proof of durable inclusion.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: ILO's official September 2026 PROSPECTS results page was reviewed for partnership composition, programme horizon, the shift toward development-centred solutions, labour-market inclusion, social protection, local economic development, enterprise access, and national-system framing.
